points.description: States that the network weights are initialized randomly (with different values) and arranged in the required topology/lattice. Equivalent wording such as 'set random initial weights in the SOM grid' earns the mark.

levels.says: Mentions only random initialization or only arranging weights in the required topology, not both.

points.description: Samples an input vector from the input space and identifies the winning neuron by similarity matching (the best-matching unit). Equivalent wording such as 'find the closest neuron to the input' earns the mark.

levels.says: Mentions only sampling an input or only finding the winning neuron, not both.

points.description: Updates the weights of the winning neuron and its neighbours, where the neighbours are determined by the neighbourhood function. Accept equivalent wording such as 'adjust the BMU and nearby neurons'.

levels.says: Updates only the winning neuron's weights, or updates weights without identifying the winning neuron and its neighbours.

points.description: Reduces the neighbourhood and decays the learning rate/share radius, and stops when ordering/convergence is complete; otherwise repeats sampling from the input space. Accept equivalent loop-control wording such as 'shrink neighbourhood and learning rate, repeat until converged'.

levels.says: Mentions only the decay/reduction of parameters or only the stop/repeat condition, not both.

rubric.notes: Full marks require a pseudo-code outline that initializes the SOM, samples an input and finds the winning neuron, updates the winner and its neighbours, and decays the neighbourhood/learning rate while repeating until convergence. Part marks are given when one of these stages is missing or only vaguely stated. No marks are earned for an unrelated algorithm or for an answer with no SOM training loop.
